transport: 4-terminal block marked "EXT Switch" (item 10, Fig 6.1a) · 2-wire dry contact: short terminals 1 and 2 = ON, open = OFF · or 2-wire switched DC 10–60 VDC, positive to terminal 3 and negative to terminal 4, into an internal opto-isolator · or 1-wire switched battery voltage (12/24/48 V) to terminal 3 · front-panel 3-position rocker must FIRST be pushed to the bottom "EXT. Switch" position · wiring
sharedMapEvidence: One Samlex owner's manual, 11001-PST-3000-12-24-48-0726, covers PST-3000-12, PST-3000-24 and PST-3000-48 in a single document with one layout figure (Fig 6.1a) and one external-control section (§8.7); the terminal numbering and the 10–60 VDC range are stated once for all three. PST-3000-48 is documented but was not seen at the Quebec retailers surveyed, so it is not listed as a model here.
gotchas: Open loop, exactly as the PST-1500/2000 block: input only, no feedback of any kind.

Terminal numbering differs from the PST-1500/2000 block, which is labelled S / – / +. Here it is 1/2 for the dry contact and 3(+)/4(−) for switched DC. Wiring a PST-3000 from a PST-1500 drawing will not work.
Switched-DC range is 10–60 VDC here versus 10–33 VDC on the PST-1500/2000. Opto-isolated, reverse-polarity protected, 1 A fuse required close to the source.

§8.7 explicitly states there is NO battery drain when the inverter is switched off by opening the external contact — unlike switching off from the RC-300, which leaves 3 mA (PST-3000-12), 5 mA (-24) or 7 mA (-48) flowing. For an unattended cabin the relay on this block is the correct kill, not the remote.
The rocker must be in the EXT position or the external control is dead, and that condition is not observable over the wire.
